dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: How is everything down there? Did you encounter any danger?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Describe your experiences to Muning.)

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Ah, I see. That does sound rather dangerous. I'm afraid I'll have to ask you to help take care of Jinwu and Zhiqiong, then.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Aren't you supposed to stop me?

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Well, that is my duty, yes. But you always run off too quickly for me to stop you, so I can't.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: All goes well, don't you fret.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: That's good, that's good. As long as things go well, the Qixing will have no reason to come down too hard on me...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I don't run that fast.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: No, you do. That's what the report says, and what the report says is the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Alright, guess I'm really, really fast, then.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Exactly. As such, please do be careful.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Resumption of work for the miners and provisions for their food, the changing of Millelith guards, contract signings, equipment overhauls, and weekly reports...

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Ah, it's you. Do you need me to help with anything else? I mean, I am a bit... busy, right now, but...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're that busy, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: You bet. There's so much work to be done that I reckon that I'll start losing hair over it soon.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: But there's nothing for it: the resumption of work at The Chasm is good for Liyue as a whole, of that there is no doubt. But the deluge of work will always have to be taken up by an unfortunate few.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Still, you have my thanks. Things are busy here, sure, but it's much improved from how things were when it was just Zhiqiong and a couple others.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I don't need help at the moment.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Phew. Well, that's good.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Not that I don't want to help you, obviously, but I'm just... a bit swamped at the moment.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: The Feiyun Commerce Guild's representative just left, and now we need to send people to put up recruitment notices for miners.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Once we're done here, I'm gonna apply for some leave.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: See you. Again, the Ministry of Civil Affairs thanks you for your efforts.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How's Zhiqiong...

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Ah yes. About Zhiqiong, the Millelith should have received news about her. If nothing goes awry, the search-and-rescue team from the Ministry should also arrive soon.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: We should have news of her shortly.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: That said, she's so fond of adventure that she probably went gallivanting somewhere by herself. *cough* If you meet her out there, please be sure to tell me.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: I'm sure you must be much busier than me, but you know, it would be nice if you could look out for her on my behalf...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I will.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Thank you. I look forward to hearing from you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's the situation with Zhiqiong?

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: The search-and-rescue team hasn't had news of her yet. But please don't panic... This isn't the time to panic just yet.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: We should have news of her shortly.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: As for me, I believe that she's still alive. Adventurers are a tough lot, so she shouldn't... Um, sorry...

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: *cough* But if you do meet her out there, please be sure to tell me.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: May I ask for your name?

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: My apologies, but The Chasm has been closed indefinitely. We do not take guests here.

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: Unless...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Unless...?

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: Unless you can get permission from Yujing Terrace... Or if you are on a <color=#00E1FFFF>special commission</color>.

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: However, things have been quite unusual lately, and our bosses have been most busy... I'd advise that you mind your own business, lest you disturb them.

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: Please leave at once. This is for your own safety.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You still owe Lan Mora for drinks. Don't you forget that.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Eh? Oh, so that's what you're here for? Hmph... Alright, alright. These adventurers... Can't ever trust them to come out and speak their minds.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Alright, then. If you have any questions, ask away. I will answer them — provided that I know the answer.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Here's the Mora that Xingqiu said he'd lend you.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Oh my! As expected of Liyue's great hero — coming in the nick of time to my aid!

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: *cough* Uh, I mean, considering your long-term partnership with the Ministry of Civil Affairs, just ask me any questions you might have.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could you tell me more about The Chasm?

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Right, so about the Chasm... If you don't intend to leave just yet, you're free to explore the area a bit. But please do keep your actions within the remit of Liyue's laws and statutes.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: I should mention, though, that there is a place that I highly recommend you avoid.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: For example, the great mine in the center of The Chasm has had a Seven-Star Array cast over it... By which I mean exactly what I say — it is a seal placed over the area by the Qixing.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, that's quite the clear explanation.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: As for the weak... I mean, focal point of the array, it lies in the Bedrock Keys surrounding the area. These were placed by the Qixing themselves. Connected in series, they affix the energy flowing through the array.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: The area around the Bedrock Keys has seen an abnormal amount of Geo elemental coalescences. It's almost as if the "thing" beneath yearns to finally emerge...

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: ...Uh, never mind me, I was just talking to myself. So yes, that's how things are. Please do not — and I repeat, do not — go near the Seven-Star Array, and don't even think about going down there to explore.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: The Bedrock Keys are definitely not losing structural integrity, and the surrounding areas are most certainly not plagued by any strange Geo elemental convergences. So please, don't you think of doing anything at all.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But...

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Hmph, I know what you're going to ask.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: There are most certainly no precious treasures down there, nor are there any prehistoric fossils to be had. And banish any thoughts you have about giant ancient ruins... Yes, please do not bear any fruitless expectations toward this place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The way you're saying all this is super suspicious!

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Not even mushrooms will grow down there! Nor are there wish-granting stones! And there are definitely no sailors who grow strong just by eating mushrooms! Again, do not get your hopes up!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, yeah, sure! There's no need to be so fierce...

choices.text: Anything else I should look out for?

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: I suggest that you go speak to Zhiqiong first. She is an adventurer hired by the Ministry and was once a miner here. She knows The Chasm's geography like the back of her hand...

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: Also, let me write you a certification real quick. When she sees it, she'll know that you're trustworthy.

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: That said, I must warn you that Zhiqiong is definitely not the sort of person who has trouble standing still, and definitely has no thoughts of undoing the array and having a look underground.

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: So there's no way that she would ever put a team of idle adventurers together to brazenly enter hazardous areas! As such, you can forget about asking her to help you enter The Chasm's mines.

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: Did... did you really?

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: As long as you understand, we're good, in which case, I won't take up any more of your time.

choices.text: Got it, then. Come, Paimon, let's go.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup, let's go!

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: Wait! I haven't finished!

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Ten crates of meat, ten crates of vegetables, various amounts of firewood and camping equipment to be given to the Millelith outpost... Three crates of various ores to be sent to the Huishan Hall warehouse in exchange for spare parts for tools... in various amounts...

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Alright, sorry for making you wait. What do you need... Ah, it's you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Since when were we all that familiar with you...?

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: I mean, you are the heroes who saved Liyue. Your deeds are remembered by us all.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Since you're here at The Chasm, you must be here on some important business. In which case, I'm sure you must have a permit from Lady Keqing, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We don't.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Really? I mean, sorry to trouble you... Since you must be very familiar with Lady Ningguang, a permit from her might hold still more weight. Could I see it, please?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, we don't have that, either.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Well, the Lord Tianshu is reclusive yet approachable, and also has great vision and the good of the people at heart. Surely he was the one who gave you permission to enter the Chasm, then?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: May... maybe?

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: In that case, would you mind letting me see your papers?

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Huh, I guess you don't have that, either. Well, Ms. Ganyu works at Yujing Terrace, supporting the Qixing directly, so I'm sure her opinion would be in lockstep with theirs. You at least have her permission, don't you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Actually, you know what? We could have just asked Ganyu to sign off on this!)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I can, uh, go look for her right now...

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: *sigh* ...

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: So... you've come at a bad time. This is really not the season to be visiting The Chasm. The Ministry of Civil Affairs is still working on eliminating a great safety hazard within, so this is still very much a danger zone.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: If you have been commissioned by some merchant to urge us to open the mine faster, then I suggest you read the report I submitted to Shenglu Hall carefully.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, what's this person talking about, exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, about Lan...

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Ah, did she tell you about some "special commission"? Well, I am the representative of the Ministry in this place, and as far as they are concerned, any commissions from the Adventurers' Guild hold no weight here.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: So you can't... I mean, don't you also try using her to put pressure on me. It won't work...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Pfft. That wasn't convincing at all!

choices.text: I mean, you do owe her money for liquor...

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: Alright! Alright! Can we change the topic, please? Let's get back down to business!

choices.text: "Also"? I take it that someone's done this to you before?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, about Xu...

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: I've been friends with the two young masters of the family he serves for a long time. The younger of them, Xingqiu, is a warm-hearted and chivalrous soul for someone of his age. I was definitely right to put my faith in him.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Of course, I also have you and Xu to thank in this case... *sigh* If this sum hadn't come in this month, I'd have some trouble making ends meet before my next payday.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Either way, I can now start worrying about next month's expenditures.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Man, how much Mora does this guy owe...

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Heh, well, old habits die hard, you know?

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: But to be honest, I haven't had the time to go to Yanshang Teahouse in a long while Not since I got assigned here, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: It's just that old debts still need paying, you know? I... guess I'll have to trouble all of you in the future as well.

choices.text: You should probably manage your finances better.

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: *sigh* You're right. I suppose I just don't consider these things enough.

choices.text: You shouldn't waste the goodwill of your friends.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: What happened? He was absent this morning during the headcount. Where on earth is he?

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: If the higher-ups find out... I'd be toast.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Ah, you're here. Good timing...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What happened? Why are you sighing?

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: *sigh* To tell you the truth, a miner from our camp went missing.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: The Chasm has a complex environment. Though things have stabilized a bit lately, it's still dangerous deep inside. So, we made it a rule to take a headcount every morning and evening.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Qi Ding — the guy who never misses a chance to brag about his daughter — was absent last night.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: During the headcount, other miners said that they had just met him and that he might return very soon. So I let it go.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: But this morning, he was still nowhere to be found. Other miners looked evasive, so I pressed them for an honest answer. It turned out that Qi Ding hadn't returned the whole night...

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Now we're in big trouble. Don't tell me it's happening again...

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: *sigh* This is something that only Ministry personnel should know.

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: But since you're the hero who saved Liyue, I think I can make an exception for you.

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: This was before The Chasm was sealed... At first, it was just a strange rumor among miners that something in The Chasm could "make their wish come true."

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: We had warned them to report to Huishan Hall should they encounter anything unusual.

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: Yet some miners tried their luck — They went looking for "The Chasm's Bounty" in secret and ended up going missing one by one.

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: When we found them some while later, they'd all gone pretty insane. It took quite some time for them to recover. That was creepy. After the incident, the Qixing decided to seal The Chasm.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Could the missing miner be...

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: Yes, I suspect Qi Ding got himself into the same situation.

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: Should anything happen to him, I'll definitely lose my job. *sigh* What's more, his wife passed away many years ago, and his daughter is now an intern at the Ministry of Civil Affairs. If we can't find him...

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: #*sigh* {NICKNAME}, I'm gonna have people put up some missing person posters, but can you help me look for him...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sure.

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: Mm, let me think if there's anything noticeable about him. He used to be on the demolitions team, there's always a strong gunpowder smell on him... Hope you find this useful.

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: #*sigh* Qi Ding, I warned you not to go down. You aren't like {NICKNAME}...
